JUDGMENT Wife and children of Murthy filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.60,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A- 9613 alleging that on 24.02.2022 at 8.00 p.m., when Murthy was sitting by the side of a road at Hosahalli Main road, JJR Nagar towards Oblesh Colony, near Rayapuram Arch, driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613, drove the same negligently dashed the same to Murthy, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Murthy.
Immediately after the accident, Murthy has been admitted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he succumbed to the injuries.
2. As on the date of accident deceased Murthy being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/-
per month by working as Autorickshaw driver.
3.

Regarding accident Magadi road traffic police registered a case in crime No.14/2022.
4.

In response to the notice, respondent No.1 Insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of the deceased.
By filing application, respondent No.1 inserted the pleading that Murthy was under intoxication during incident and the deceased Murthy was the sole responsible for the accident.
In the written statement dated 21.11.2024, the respondent No.1 asserted non production of Inquest Report by the petitioners to show their relationship with deceased Murthy, S/o.Nallappa.
5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 owner of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 appeared through his advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 09.01.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 24.02.2022 at about 08.00 p.m., in Hosahalli Main Road, near Rayapuram Arch in Bengaluru, when the deceased Lakshmi Narasamma vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144321776/

2.

On 30.08.2023, 14.09.2023, 21.01.2025,
petitioners produced evidence of Obalesh and Kumar as P.Ws.2 and 3 and produced 3 documents at Ex.P.16, P.17 and P.20.

On 05.02.2024, 01.10.2024 respondent No.1-Insurance Company produced the evidence of MRO, Victoria Hospital and Officer of Insurance Company as R.Ws.1 and 2 and produced 6 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.6.
8.
During pendency of the petition, petitioner No.2- Basavaraju, S/o.Murthy expired.
9. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.17,33,104/- with current and future interest at 6%p.a. from the respondents as compensation.

when her husband Murthy was sitting by the side of a road on Hosahalli Main road, JJR Nagar towards Oblesh Colony, near Rayapuram Arch, driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613, drove the same negligently dashed the same to Murthy, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Murthy.

P.W.1 stated that, Immediately after the accident,
Murthy has been shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he succumbed to the injuries.
12.

In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that Murthy who was under the influence of alcohol during the alleged incident, was the sole responsible for the alleged incident.

P.W.1 stated that she neither witnessed the accident nor visited the place of accident.
P.W.1 stated that her husband was sitting by the side of the road.

In the evidence affidavit P.W.2 - Obalesh stated that on 24.02.2022 at 8.00 p.m. when he was standing with his friends by the side of the road, at JJR Nagar towards Oblesh Colony, deceased was sitting on the side of Hosahalli Main Road, near Rayapuram Arch, driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613, drove the same negligently made the wheels to run on the legs of deceased, resulting in fracture injuries to both legs of the deceased Murthy.
P.W.2 stated that immediately after the accident, deceased has been shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he succumbed to the injuries on 25.02.2022 at 3.10 a.m.

In the evidence, P.W.2 produced the copy of his statement recorded by the police and copy of his bank passbook at Ex.P.16 and P.17.
16.
In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated that brother of deceased namely Nagendra has lodged the complaint to the police.
P.W.2 submitted ignorance about since how many hours the deceased was siting on the side of the road.
P.W.2 stated that he was in the spot for about 45 minutes and during that time the deceased was sitting there.
P.W.2 stated that Kumar - younger brother of deceased shifted the deceased to hospital.
P.W.2 denied the suggestion that deceased was sleeping on the road by consuming alcohol.

P.W.2 denied the suggestion that in order to take left turn, the vehicles have to move slowly at the accident spot and the accident occurred due to fault of the deceased and there was no fault on the part of the driver of Bolero vehicle.
17. In the evidence affidavit P.W.3 - Kumar S/o.Nallappa stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

18. In the evidence affidavit R.W.1 - Medical Record Technician of Victoria hospital produced copy of MLC Register extract, Police Intimation and Case Sheet at Ex.R.2 to R.4.

22. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records and medical records regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

23. Hence, I have concluded that on 24.02.2022 at 8.00 p.m. when Murthy was lying or sitting by the side of Hosahalli Main road, JJR Nagar towards Obalesh Colony, near Rayapuram Arch under intoxication, Krishnamurthy, S/o.Venkataramanappa, negligently drove the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613, made the wheels of Bolero vehicle to run over Murthy, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to lower limbs of Murthy, who succumbed to those injuries at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

24. Issue No.2: In the evidence P.W.1 stated that as on the date of accident, Murthy being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month by working as driver of Autorickshaw and used to contribute entire income to the family.
25. In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding relationship of petitioners and deceased, age, occupation and income of the deceased Murthy.
25. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted ignorance to the question that at the time of accident her her husband was aged more than 45 years.
P.W.1 stated that Murthy was younger to her and submitted ignorance about the age of her deceased son i.e., 2 nd petitioner.
In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted inability to produce Driving Licence extract of her husband.

In the evidence dated 21.1.2025 P.W.1 produced digitally signed Family Tree certificate issued by Deputy Tahsildar, City Circle Hobli, dated 15.01.2025 at Ex.P.19.
26.
In the evidence P.W.2 stated nothing regarding age, occupation, income of the deceased.
27. In the evidence affidavit P.W.3-Kumar, S/o.Nallappa stated that petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife and children of Murthy.
In the evidence P.W.3 produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.20.
In the cross-examination, P.W.3 stated that before police he has stated that petitioner No.1 is his sister-in-law i.e. wife of his elder brother - Murthy.
28. In the evidence R.W.1 and 2 stated nothing regarding relationship between petitioners and deceased, age, occupation and income of deceased Murthy.

sentences.text: In the P.M.Report and Inquest Mahazar age of the deceased is noted as 35 years.
In the copy of the Aadhar cards marked at Ex.P.10 to 12, name of Murthy is noted as husband and father of petitioner No.1 to 3 respectively.
In the MLC Register extract and death summary, age of the deceased is noted as 47 years.
In Family Tree certificate marked at Ex.P.19, name of the petitioners are mentioned as wife and children of Murthy.
30. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by petitioners regarding their relationship with the deceased Murthy.
In the file, there are no documents regarding occupation and income of Murthy.

31. Hence, I have inferred that, it is fit and proper to calculate the compensation under the head of loss of dependency, presuming that as on the date of incident deceased Murthy being aged about 47 years, used to earn approximately Rs.15,500/- p.m. and used to contribute 2/3rd of his income to the family, by applying multiplier '13', in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Murthy as on the - 47 years date of incident - Notional monthly income of deceased - Rs.15,500/- Murthy as on the date of accident Less: 1/3rd towards personal expenses - Rs.10,334/- of the deceased Murthy (15,500/- - 5,166/- = 10,334/-) Annual income of the deceased - Rs.1,24,008/-
 10,334/- x12  Multiplier Applicable - 13  Loss of dependency 1,24,008/- x 13 - Rs.16,12,104/-
32.

As referred above, in the file, there are no documents to show that as on the date of incident, Murthy had permanent occupation and permanent quantum of income and medical record shows that during incident, Murthy was under intoxication.
Hence no money is added towards future prospects while calculation of compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

Hence, I award Rs.16,12,104/-
towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/-
towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/- towards loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 3 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.

33. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife and daughter of deceased Murthy are entitle to receive Rs.17,33,104/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.

Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 petitioners No.1 & 3 at Rs.44,000/each Total 17,33,104-00 34.
In the written statement Respondent No.1 Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 as on the date of accident.
Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.4 shows that as on the date of incident, respondent No.1 is the insurer of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA- 41-A-9613.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.2 owner of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.17,33,104/- (Rupees Seventeen lakhs Thirty Three thousand one hundred and four only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioner equally.
After deposit, 50% of the compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner No.1 and 3 by crediting the same to their bank account directly.

Surplus compensation amount with interest allotted to petitioner No.1 and 3 shall be deposited in any bank in the name of petitioner No.1 and 3 for a period of 3 years without permitting to create any encumbrances.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer-I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 11th day of March, 2025.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.

Hence no money is added towards future prospects while calculation of compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence, I award Rs.16,12,104/-
towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/-
towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/- towards loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 3 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.
Head of Compensation Amount/Rs Lakshmi Narasamma vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144321776/
In the written statement Respondent No.1 Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.2 owner of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.KA-41-A-9613 has violated any terms of the policy.

Surplus compensation amount with interest allotted to petitioner No.1 and 3 shall be deposited in any bank in the name of petitioner No.1 and 3 for a period of 3 years without permitting to create any encumbrances.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
